summary: Explains that ad hoc commands suit rarely repeated tasks, gives the general syntax `ansible [pattern] -m [module] -a "[module options]"`, and notes that `-a` accepts key=value or a JSON string.
questions: When should I use an ad hoc command instead of writing a playbook?
What's the basic syntax of an ansible ad hoc command?
Can I pass JSON to the -a option for complex module arguments?

answer_card.title: Ad hoc command syntax
answer_card.answer_md:
Use ad hoc commands for things you do rarely (e.g. powering off lab machines before a vacation).
```bash
ansible [pattern] -m [module] -a "[module options]"
```
`-a` accepts either `key=value` pairs or a JSON string wrapped in `{ }` for more complex options.
